title: Sparrowline Dispatch LLM integration — raw capture
content:
Context: first technical handshake with Sparrowline (Freight/last-mile dispatch). Customer evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for low-latency dispatch suggestions + on-device fallback. Notes are unpolished — capturing constraints, gotchas, and immediate next steps.

Call metadata:
- Date: 2025-11-03 (initial call), follow-up 2026-02-28 sync
- Attendees: Maya Chen (RWD SE), Ravi Patel (RWD Solutions), Aisha Gomez (Sparrowline Eng PM), Samir Rao (Sparrowline SRE), Jorge (Sparrowline ops lead)
- Channel: Zoom (recorded), initial slide deck link in Jira ticket ENG-1347

High-level ask from Sparrowline:
- Real-time dispatch suggestion for drivers (~1–3 candidate actions per event) when delivery exception occurs (traffic, address mismatch).
- Latency target: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 200ms in their US-west regions; baseline now ~600ms using cloud-hosted model.
- Throughput: peak 300 reqs/sec (burst to 1k for holiday windows).
- Data residency: must stay within their VPC (Private deployment) and PII redaction enforced upstream.
- Offline mode: limited cell coverage — need degraded local fallback (small model or cached policy) for 30–60s outages.

Technical constraints they highlighted:
- On-prem network: NAT with strict egress; allowlist required for control-plane callbacks.
- GPU estate: currently a single DGX-like node (A100 x8) managed by their infra team; they want an initial POC on a single node with room to scale to multi-node pool.
- Storage: NFS-backed model store with conservative IOPS; prefer small (50–100 MiB) artifact pulls vs large disk images.
- Auth: corporate SSO -> they want OIDC + SCIM for user provisioning to console.
- Telemetry: must forward audit logs to Splunk; 30d retention minimum.

Prompting / model expectations:
- Candidate generation + rerank pipeline: fast candidate gen (local quantized model) + rerank on higher-quality model in the private cluster.
- Need deterministic rerank for A/B consistency (seeded sampling disabled for rerank).
- Domain-specific glossary: driver nicknames, route codes (R-1234), and local place names — risk of hallucination when model not fine-tuned.

Gotchas / Risks called out during call:
1) Tokenization mismatch: their carrier codes include slashes and mixed-case — test shows off-by-one token splits using base tokenizer. Action: validate tokenization on representative payloads.
2) Network egress policy: their security team will block unknown control-plane endpoints; we may have to support a fully air-gapped control plane or work via site-to-site VPN.
3) Cold-start model pulls: NFS IO limits mean pulling 8GB model images will disrupt other infra — prefer staged chunked downloads or using quantized smaller artifacts.
4) KV cache invalidation: their workflow updates driver status rapidly; need strong cache TTL and KV eviction rules to avoid suggesting already-completed actions.
5) Offline fallback: customer expects consistent UX — need a small on-device policy (<=300MB) with graceful reconciliation when connectivity returns (duplicate suppression).

Immediate technical validation tasks (RWD + Sparrowline):
- Maya / Ravi: produce a tokenization test set (20–30 sample payloads) by 2025-11-10. (Assigned)
- Sparrowline devs: share a sanitized sample stream (1-hour compressed trace) with event types and example payloads by 2025-11-14. (Assigned to Samir)
- SRE check: confirm NAT/allowlist requirements and outbound IP stability (Samir) — due 2025-11-12.
- Infra: run quick disk IO benchmark on NFS mount and report sustained IOPS and latency; recommend model artifact pull strategy afterwards.

POC plan (sketch):
Phase 0 — Validation (2 weeks)
- Tokenization tests, sample payloads, simple latency profiling using hosted small models to set baseline.
- Confirm allowlist/egress plan and audit log sink options.

Phase 1 — Local POC (3–4 weeks)
- Deploy Redwood Private minimal stack to their VPC (control-plane can be remote if allowlist ok).
- Use quantized 7B candidate gen (local) + 13B reranker in Private cluster.
- Simulated load testing up to 500 req/s (synthetic traces). Measure 95p latency end-to-end.

Phase 2 — Resilience + Offline (2 weeks)
- Implement small cached policy (200–300MB) as offline fallback, test reconciliation logic, duplicate suppression approach.
- KV cache tuning: TTLs, write-through to persistent store.

Phase 3 — Production rollout (TBD)
- Autoscaling for peak holiday windows, SLA targets, ops runbook, runbook for network failovers.

Open questions (need answers before engineering kickoff):
- Q1: Is full air-gapped control plane an absolute requirement or negotiable? (security)
- Q2: What is acceptable cold-start time for model warmup? They implied <= 60s for small models, <=5min for large reranker — need to confirm exactly.
- Q3: Splunk ingestion specifics: do they want raw token-level logs or only telemetry/metadata? Data retention concerns.
- Q4: Reconciliation priority: when offline suggestions executed, what is authoritative source (driver app vs central system)?

Proposed short-term deliverables (owner -> ETA):
- Tokenization test report (Maya) -> 2025-11-10
- Sanitized sample hour trace (Samir) -> 2025-11-14
- NFS IO benchmark (Sparrowline infra) -> 2025-11-12 (urgent)
- Draft POC infra diagram + allowlist requirements (Ravi) -> 2025-11-16
- Draft offline fallback spec (Maya + Aisha) -> 2025-11-20

Notes to self / SE tips:
- Bring a small quantized persona (gptq 3-bit) for candidate gen demo to reduce pull sizes.
- Pre-warm the reranker with a short-lived in-memory cache keyed by route-id to shave 15–30ms for repeat events.
- Use prefix caching aggressively for driver history — prefix hits will cover many repaired-route cases.

Meeting cadence: weekly sync on Fridays 10am PT until POC complete.

Slack threads to link later: #sparrowline-onramp (create), #rwd-private-deploys.

Misc scribbles (raw):
- Jorge says drivers complain when suggestions change mid-delivery — need deterministic reranking + sticky suggestion id.
- Aisha: "we can tolerate up to 3% suggestion divergence vs legacy rules" — record as tolerance threshold.
- Look into using model distillation to create 200–300MB fallback policy (distill from reranker).

Next steps (today):
- Send follow-up email with required artifacts and proposed POC plan (Maya).
- Open Jira ENG-1347 tasks for tokenization tests and infra benchmarking (Ravi).

-- end of raw capture --
